_comment: 议题投票数据。candidates=未辩候选(供投票)，debated=已辩(链到辩论)。每个候选的 giscus 讨论 term = 'topic:'+id；净票 = 👍 − 👎(其他表情不计)。votes 字段由 routine 每次跑时用 `gh api graphql` 读 GitHub Discussions 的 👍/👎 回写净票(页面据此显示；点开卡片则加载实时 giscus)。另有一个 term='open-questions' 的讨论(页面『提个新议题』)收观众自提议题——routine 把里面好的提案提炼成新 candidates。新候选议题加进 candidates 即可。

candidates.q: 「只专注于你能控制的」是处世智慧，还是一种对改不了的不公视而不见的特权式逃避？
candidates.q_en: Is 'focus only on what you can control' practical wisdom, or a privileged way of looking past injustice you could help change?
candidates.note: 斯多葛的控制二分法是定力，还是退让？专注可控能安顿内心，但面对结构性不公，它会不会变成一种体面的逃避甚至共谋？
candidates.note_en: Is the Stoic dichotomy of control composure, or quietism? Focusing on the controllable settles the mind — but against structural injustice, can it curdle into a respectable dodge, even complicity?

candidates.q: 现在的年轻人（尤其在亚洲）为什么不想生孩子？这对个人与社会意味着什么？
candidates.q_en: Why don't young people — especially in Asia — want children anymore, and what does it mean for the individual and for society?
candidates.note: 不只是房价与内卷——从贝克尔的家庭经济学、波伏娃对母职的批判、东亚的升学军备竞赛，到贝纳塔尔的反生育主义与阿伦特的『诞生性』；而少子化对老龄社会、养老金、代际契约又意味着什么。
candidates.note_en: More than housing costs and the rat race — from Becker's economics of the family and Beauvoir's critique of motherhood to East Asia's education arms race, Benatar's antinatalism, and Arendt's 'natality'; and what a birth dearth means for aging societies, pensions, and the intergenerational contract.

candidates.q: 儒、释、道的异同：三家分歧究竟在哪，又在何处殊途同归？
candidates.q_en: Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism: where do the three traditions truly differ, and where do they converge?
candidates.note: 中国思想的三根支柱：儒家入世尽伦、道家顺其自然、佛家解脱出世——它们对『自我、欲望、社会、生死』各执什么主张？分歧之外，又为何能『三教合一』、在同一个人身上并存？
candidates.note_en: The three pillars of Chinese thought: Confucian engagement with the world, Daoist going-with-nature, Buddhist liberation beyond it — what does each hold about the self, desire, society, and death? And beyond their differences, why have the 'three teachings' so often merged and coexisted within one person?

candidates.q: 东方与西方哲学：源头何以不同，如何塑造了今天的东西方人，又能否融合双方的智慧？
candidates.q_en: Eastern and Western philosophy: why did they diverge at the root, how have they shaped people East and West today, and can the two wisdoms be fused?
candidates.note: 雅斯贝尔斯的『轴心时代』里，希腊求逻各斯与分析、追问「世界是什么」；东方重关系、整体与「人该如何活」——一边长出个体、科学与权利意识，一边长出关系自我、和谐与修身。这两套源头如何造就了今天东西方人的思维差异？又能否取长补短、合一而非择一？
candidates.note_en: In Jaspers's 'Axial Age,' Greece pursued logos, analysis, and 'what is the world'; the East prized relation, the whole, and 'how should one live' — one growing the individual, science, and rights, the other the relational self, harmony, and self-cultivation. How did these two roots shape the minds of modern East and West, and can their strengths be fused rather than chosen between?

candidates.q: “忠于真实的自我”是不是个伪命题？到底有没有一个本真的我？
candidates.q_en: Is 'being true to yourself' even coherent — is there a real self to be true to?
candidates.note: 人设与真心、该不该装——萨特『自欺』、海德格尔本真性、佛教无我、社会角色论，质问那个『真实的我』到底存不存在。
candidates.note_en: Masks versus the 'real you,' whether to perform or stay raw — Sartre's 'bad faith,' Heidegger's authenticity, Buddhist no-self, and role theory all interrogate whether that 'true self' exists at all.

candidates.q: 什么样的不平等是可以接受的？
candidates.q_en: What kind of inequality is acceptable?
candidates.note: 机会平等就够了吗？多大的差距是公正、多大是不义？——马克思、哈耶克、亚当·斯密各执一词。
candidates.note_en: Is equal opportunity enough? How much gap is just, how much is wrong? — Marx, Hayek and Adam Smith disagree.

candidates.q: 为什么我们忍不住跟别人比？嫉妒能消除吗？
candidates.q_en: Why can't we stop comparing ourselves to others — and can envy ever be cured?
candidates.note: 社媒时代最普遍的痛——基拉尔『模仿欲望』、庄子、叔本华、社会比较理论，拆解我们为何总盯着别人、又如何停下。
candidates.note_en: The most universal ache of the social-media age — Girard's 'mimetic desire,' Zhuangzi, Schopenhauer, and social-comparison theory unpack why we keep watching others, and how to stop.

candidates.q: 我们的成功与失败，多少是「应得的」？努力真能决定命运吗？
candidates.q_en: How much of our success or failure do we actually deserve — and does effort really decide our fate?
candidates.note: 『为什么我这么拼还不行』背后的大问题——桑德尔『精英的傲慢』、罗尔斯无知之幕、儒家修身、『王侯将相宁有种乎』，争运气与应得的边界。
candidates.note_en: The big question behind 'why am I grinding this hard and still falling short' — Sandel's 'tyranny of merit,' Rawls's veil of ignorance, Confucian self-cultivation, and the ancient cry 'are kings and nobles born to it?' — over where luck ends and desert begins.

candidates.q: 我们对远方陌生人的苦难，负有多大义务？
candidates.q_en: How much do we owe the suffering of distant strangers?
candidates.note: 溺水孩童的思想实验、有效利他主义，对上『亲疏有别』的常识道德——义务有没有半径？
candidates.note_en: Singer's drowning-child thought experiment and effective altruism against the common-sense morality of concentric circles — does obligation have a radius?

candidates.q: 美，是主观感受，还是有客观的标准？
candidates.q_en: Is beauty just in the eye of the beholder, or is there an objective standard?
candidates.note: 从柏拉图的理念、苏轼的意境，到康德的『无目的的合目的性』与当代神经美学——美到底是什么。
candidates.note_en: From Plato's Forms and Su Shi's poetic mood to Kant's 'purposiveness without purpose' and today's neuroaesthetics — what is beauty, really?

candidates.q: 数学是被发现的，还是被发明的？
candidates.q_en: Is mathematics discovered, or invented?
candidates.note: 柏拉图说数学在理念世界里现成等着被发现，也有人说它只是人类心智的发明——一个关于实在本质的老问题。
candidates.note_en: Plato says math waits to be discovered in a realm of Forms; others say it's merely an invention of the human mind — an old question about the nature of reality.

candidates.q: 我们该如何面对死亡？如何做到「向死而生」？
candidates.q_en: How should we face death — and how do we actually live 'toward' it (being-toward-death)?
candidates.note: 伊壁鸠鲁说『死亡与我们无关』，庄子鼓盆而歌，海德格尔说向死而生，佛陀谈无常——直面终点。
candidates.note_en: Epicurus says 'death is nothing to us,' Zhuangzi drummed and sang, Heidegger speaks of being-toward-death, the Buddha on impermanence — facing the end.

candidates.q: 我们对地球（其他物种、后代）负有怎样的义务？
candidates.q_en: What do we owe the Earth — other species, and future generations?
candidates.note: 对其他物种、对尚未出生的后代——我们凭什么索取，又欠下什么？
candidates.note_en: Toward other species and generations not yet born — by what right do we take, and what do we owe?

candidates.q: 自由与平等不可兼得时，该牺牲哪个？
candidates.q_en: When liberty and equality can't both be had, which should give way?
candidates.note: 自由市场的效率与不平等，还是再分配的公平与强制？现代政治的核心取舍。
candidates.note_en: The efficiency-and-inequality of free markets, or the fairness-and-coercion of redistribution? The central trade-off of modern politics.

candidates.q: 人是否拥有真正的自由意志？
candidates.q_en: Do humans have genuine free will?
candidates.note: 我们是真的在选，还是基因、大脑与处境替我们选了？——决定论与能动性之争。
candidates.note_en: Do we really choose, or do genes, brain and circumstance choose for us? — determinism versus agency.

candidates.q: 我们为何系统性地低估『照护与情感劳动』的价值？（带孩子、陪伴、安抚、协调——这些撑起一切却没人记功的活）
candidates.q_en: Why do we systematically undervalue care and emotional labor?
candidates.note: 带孩子、陪伴老人、安抚、协调、记住每个人的状态——这些撑起一切却没人记功的活，为什么总被当成『不算工作』？努斯鲍姆、波伏娃、亚当·斯密、涂尔干各执一端。
candidates.note_en: Raising children, tending the old, soothing, coordinating, remembering everyone's state — the work that holds everything up yet earns no credit. Why is it forever treated as 'not really work'? Nussbaum, Beauvoir, Adam Smith, and Durkheim take different sides.

candidates.q: 拖延症要治吗？deadline 是第一生产力，重要的事最后也赶得出来——那它到底是不是病？
candidates.q_en: Does procrastination even need fixing? Deadlines are the ultimate motivator and the important stuff still ships — so is it really a flaw?
candidates.note: 反常识地问：拖延也许不是意志缺陷，而是大脑的优先级调度？但赶 deadline 的代价、焦虑与质量折损又该怎么算——到底治还是不治。
candidates.note_en: A contrarian question: maybe procrastination isn't a failure of will but the brain's way of triaging priorities? Yet the cost of the last-minute crunch — the anxiety, the quality you trade away — still has to be reckoned. Cure it, or not?

candidates.q: 真爱是发现的，还是培养（甚至建构）出来的？
candidates.q_en: Is true love found, or cultivated — even constructed?
candidates.note: 柏拉图的会饮、叔本华眼里繁衍的诡计、波伏娃对浪漫爱的批判、阿德勒『被爱不如会爱』——爱到底是什么。
candidates.note_en: Plato's Symposium, Schopenhauer's trick of the species, Beauvoir's critique of romantic love, Adler's 'better to love than to be loved' — what love really is.

candidates.q: 维系和谐，有时是否比说出真相更重要？
candidates.q_en: Is keeping the peace sometimes more important than telling the truth?
candidates.note: 苏格拉底为真理赴死，孔子讲『和』，阿伦特谈真相与政治——在家庭、职场、社会里，何时该说、何时该忍。
candidates.note_en: Socrates died for the truth, Confucius prized harmony, Arendt on truth and politics — in family, work, and society, when to speak and when to hold back.

candidates.q: 该为过去的选择后悔吗？如何与无法重来的过去和解？
candidates.q_en: Should we regret the choices we made — and how do we make peace with a past we can't redo?
candidates.note: 『如果当初…』的内疚反复折磨人——克尔凯郭尔、斯多葛、庄子（鼓盆而歌）、佛教放下，各给一套与过去和解的办法。
candidates.note_en: The 'if only I had…' guilt that keeps gnawing — Kierkegaard, the Stoics, Zhuangzi (drumming and singing at his wife's death), and Buddhist letting-go each offer a way to make peace with what's done.

candidates.q: 国家的权力从何而来、有无正当的边界？
candidates.q_en: Where does the state's power come from, and does it have legitimate limits?
candidates.note: 社会契约、天命、还是法家的强力？权力的来源与边界，是政治哲学最古老的争点。
candidates.note_en: Social contract, the Mandate of Heaven, or Legalist force? The source and limits of legitimate power are political philosophy's oldest quarrel.

candidates.q: 有什么是金钱不该买卖的？市场该有边界吗？
candidates.q_en: Is there anything money shouldn't be able to buy? Should markets have moral limits?
candidates.note: 从代孕、器官到选票与友情——当市场逻辑渗入一切，有没有该守住的非卖品？
candidates.note_en: From surrogacy and organs to votes and friendship — as market logic seeps into everything, are there things that should stay off the auction block?

candidates.q: 大型组织里的『组织政治』，是毒瘤还是必需？普通人又该如何看待、甚至善用它？
candidates.q_en: Office politics in large organizations: a cancer, or a necessity — and how should ordinary people navigate, even use, it?
candidates.note: 升迁从来不只看业绩——办公室里有看不见的权力地图、联盟与人情账。一派说它是劣币驱逐良币的内耗毒瘤；一派说凡有人聚集、资源有限处必有政治，回避＝把话语权让人。韩非子的法术势、马基雅维利的现实政治、韦伯的科层制、孔子的正名、老子的不争各执一端——普通人该看清它、利用它，还是守拙远离？
candidates.note_en: Promotions never hinge on output alone — every office has an invisible map of power, alliances, and favors owed. One side calls it a corrosive drain that drives out the capable; the other says wherever people gather over scarce resources, politics is inevitable, and opting out just hands your voice to others. Han Feizi's statecraft, Machiavelli's realpolitik, Weber's bureaucracy, Confucius's 'rectification of names,' and Laozi's non-contention each take a side — should ordinary people see through it, use it, or keep their distance?

candidates.q: 家中老人病重、靠插管维持近乎植物人的状态，作为子女，该不该撤管放手？
candidates.q_en: An elderly parent kept alive by tubes in a near-vegetative state — should the children withdraw life support and let go?
candidates.note: 这是许多家庭真实经历过的最艰难抉择，没有标准答案。一边是『生命神圣、为人子者岂能放手』的孝与尊严；一边是『让其有尊严地解脱、不再受苦』的慈悲与生命质量之辨。儒家的孝、庄子的顺化生死、佛教的无常与慈悲、康德的生命尊严、伊壁鸠鲁『死亡与我们无关』各执一端——在『谁来决定、何为善终、放手是不是不孝』之间，子女如何自处。
candidates.note_en: One of the hardest choices many families have actually faced, with no clean answer. On one side, the sanctity of life and filial duty — how could a child let go? On the other, mercy and quality of life — letting someone be released with dignity, free of suffering. Confucian filial piety, Zhuangzi's acceptance of life and death, Buddhist impermanence and compassion, Kant's dignity of life, and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' each take a side — amid who decides, what a good death is, and whether letting go is a betrayal.

candidates.q: 企业用人，该「以德为先」还是「以才为先」？
candidates.q_en: In hiring and promotion, should an organization put character first, or ability first?
candidates.note: 司马光说『德者才之帅』，曹操却『唯才是举』——有才无德的能臣可能反噬，有德无才又难当大任。孔子的为政以德、韩非子的循名责实、现代用人讲的能力 vs 价值观契合各执一端：到底该把品行还是本事放在第一位？普通管理者招人、提拔时又如何真正权衡。
candidates.note_en: Sima Guang held that 'virtue is the commander of talent,' yet Cao Cao vowed to 'promote on talent alone' — the gifted-but-unscrupulous can turn on you, while the upright-but-incompetent can't carry the load. Confucius's rule-by-virtue, Han Feizi's accountability-by-results, and modern hiring's 'skills vs values fit' each take a side: should character or capability come first — and how does a real manager actually weigh them?

candidates.q: 下属能力或动力不足，领导该花时间 coaching，还是果断 manage out？
candidates.q_en: When a report lacks the ability or the drive, should a leader invest in coaching — or manage them out?
candidates.note: Dweck 的成长型思维与孔子『有教无类、因材施教』说人能变、值得教；Netflix 的『keeper test』与韩非子的赏罚分明说留错人是对团队的不公、机会成本高昂。关键还在于分清『能力不足』（多半可教）与『动力不足』（难补）——领导该投入辅导，还是及时止损？又怎么做到既负责又不残忍。
candidates.note_en: Dweck's growth mindset and Confucius's 'teach without discrimination, tailor to the person' say people can change and are worth coaching; Netflix's 'keeper test' and Han Feizi's strict reward-and-punishment say keeping the wrong person is unfair to the team and costly. Much turns on telling a skill gap (usually coachable) from a will gap (far harder) — should a leader invest in coaching, or cut losses in time, and how to do it responsibly without being cruel?

candidates.q: 「你眼中的别人不是别人，你眼中的自己不是自己，你眼中的别人才是自己」——这话有道理吗？
candidates.q_en: 'The others you see aren't really them, the self you see isn't really you, and the others you see are actually you' — is there truth to this?
candidates.note: 你对他人的评判往往照出的是自己——心理学的『投射』、库利的『镜中我』、世亲『万法唯识』、庄子的物我两忘，都在说我们看到的『别人』有多少是自己的影子。这句网络箴言，是深刻的自知洞见，还是把一切化约成主观投射的相对主义？
candidates.note_en: What you judge in others often mirrors yourself — psychology's 'projection,' Cooley's 'looking-glass self,' Vasubandhu's 'mind-only,' and Zhuangzi's dissolving of self and thing all suggest how much of the 'other' you see is your own shadow. A profound insight into self-knowledge, or a relativism that dissolves everything into subjective projection?

candidates.q: 我们应该永远诚实，还是可以说出善意的谎言？
candidates.q_en: Should we always be honest, or are kind lies sometimes right?
candidates.note: 康德说撒谎绝对不可、哪怕对门口的杀人犯；功利主义只看后果——能减少伤害的善意谎言未必是恶。诚实是无条件的义务，还是要让位于善意与体贴？落到日常：报喜不报忧、医生该不该告知绝症、『你今天气色真好』。
candidates.note_en: Kant said lying is never permissible — not even to the murderer at the door; consequentialists weigh outcomes — a kind lie that spares harm may be no sin. Is honesty an unconditional duty, or must it yield to kindness? In daily life: sparing bad news, whether a doctor should disclose a terminal diagnosis, 'you look great today.'

candidates.q: 普通人投资，该买大盘指数，还是买自己拿着放心的个股？
candidates.q_en: For ordinary investors: buy the broad index, or the individual stocks you can hold with confidence?
candidates.note: 指数派（博格尔、有效市场假说）说普通人跑不赢市场、低成本宽基才理性；芒格、巴菲特说留在能力圈、只买你真正懂的少数好公司；塔勒布提醒黑天鹅与脆弱性，卡尼曼则戳破『我比别人懂』的过度自信。普通人到底该认命买大盘，还是相信自己的判断？
candidates.note_en: Indexers (Bogle, the efficient-market hypothesis) say ordinary people can't beat the market — low-cost broad funds are the rational bet; Munger and Buffett say stay in your circle of competence and own only the few businesses you truly understand; Taleb warns of black swans and fragility, while Kahneman punctures the overconfidence of 'I know better.' Resign to the index, or trust your own judgment?

candidates.q: 「爱」与「被爱」，哪一种更幸福？
candidates.q_en: Which brings more happiness — to love, or to be loved?
candidates.note: 弗洛姆《爱的艺术》说爱是主动的能力、给予比索取更丰盈；阿德勒『被爱不如会爱』；亚里士多德说主动去爱比被爱更近于德性与幸福；但也有人说被全然接纳与珍视才是最深的安全感。主动付出与被珍爱，哪种让人更幸福、更自由？
candidates.note_en: Fromm's 'Art of Loving' calls love an active capacity — giving is fuller than getting; Adler held it's better to love than to be loved; Aristotle thought actively loving is closer to virtue and happiness; yet others say being fully cherished is the deepest security. Active giving or being treasured — which makes us happier and freer?

debated.q: 幸福到底是什么？我们是否应该追求幸福？
debated.q_en: What is happiness, really? And should we even pursue it?

debated.q: AI 时代，人如何夺回注意力与存在的意义？
debated.q_en: In the age of AI, how do we reclaim our attention and the meaning of our existence?

debated.q: AI 取代工作后，人类是否迎来存在危机？普通人怎样面对中年失业？
debated.q_en: After AI replaces human work, will humanity face an existential crisis? How should ordinary people cope with mass midlife unemployment?

debated.q: 原生家庭的创伤：我们多大程度被童年塑造？能否走出？能否改变父母？
debated.q_en: Trauma from the family we're born into: how much does childhood shape us, can we move past it, and can we change our parents?

debated.q: AI 与算法：在增强我们，还是在让我们退化？
debated.q_en: AI and algorithms: are they augmenting us, or making us atrophy?

debated.q: AI 时代该怎么养孩子？——拼命鸡娃、挤名校到底还值不值得？
debated.q_en: Raising kids in the age of AI: is intense “tiger parenting” and chasing elite schools still worth it?

debated.q: 科技大厂的『扁平化』——一个经理带 30–50 人，会成为常态吗？
debated.q_en: Big-tech 'flattening' — one manager over 30–50 reports: is this the new normal?

debated.q: 是否有“造物主”，如果有的话，TA为什么要造出人类？
debated.q_en: Is there a 'Creator'? And if so, why would they have made humankind?

debated.q: 一个好的『管理者』，到底是怎样的？
debated.q_en: What actually makes a good manager?

debated.q: “知道”和“做到”之间的差异是如何产生的？（知道该锻炼、早睡，却很难做到）
debated.q_en: Why is there a gap between knowing and doing? (We know we should exercise and sleep early — yet rarely do.)

debated.q: 人是否应该追求长生，如果人真的能够长生，世界会怎样？
debated.q_en: Should we pursue immortality — and if humans really could live forever, what would the world become?

debated.q: 金钱能（在多大程度上）买到幸福？
debated.q_en: Can money buy happiness — and how much?
